reason: Paper directly demonstrates that TRPM1 cation channels of retinal ON bipolar cells are the primary autoantibody target in melanoma-associated retinopathy. TRPM1 is one of the three tracked genes. The study uses Trpm1-/- mice, colocalization with GRM6-pathway markers (Grm6-GFP transgenics, Galpha-o), and retinal cell biology. Highly relevant to TRPM1, and contextually relevant to GPR179 and GRM6 as co-players in ON bipolar cell signaling.

Title 'Vector platforms for gene therapy of inherited retinopathies' directly covers the therapeutic landscape for GUCY2D (LCA1) and RPE65 (LCA2), which are the canonical first-in-class gene therapy targets for Leber congenital amaurosis. Abstract is absent but the title unambiguously places this paper at the intersection of gene therapy and the two tracked genes. Rescuing is warranted.

Calcium modulation of vertebrate phototransduction is directly relevant to both CNGA1 (cyclic nucleotide-gated channel whose gating is calcium-calmodulin modulated) and GRK1 (rhodopsin kinase whose activity is regulated by the calcium sensor recoverin). The abstract is absent and the paper is old (1994), but the subject matter is mechanistically central to both genes.

Directly studies structure-function of the GNAT1 protein (transducin alpha subunit). The paper introduces mutations in linker regions of alpha(T) and characterizes their effects on basal GDP-GTP exchange rates and cGMP phosphodiesterase activation. Core GNAT1 biochemistry.

Directly studies a gain-of-function point mutation (R238Q) in transducin-alpha (GNAT1), characterizing its effects on GTPase activity, RGS9-1 uncoupling, and effector function. This is core GNAT1 molecular biology directly relevant to the gene's functional mechanisms.

Studies native vs. reconstituted heterotrimeric transducin purified from bovine rod photoreceptor membranes. Gtalpha = GNAT1. The paper characterizes posttranslational modifications, heterotrimer stability, and interaction with rhodopsin and PDE6, all directly relevant to GNAT1 biology. RGR connection is incidental but GNAT1 relevance is strong.

This is a hematology paper characterizing isolation of human hematopoietic stem cells using AC133/CD133 (PROM1) and CD7 as surface markers. The subject is stem cell immunophenotyping and NOD/SCID engraftment. There is no retinal, ophthalmic, or visual disease content. PROM1 is used here only as a generic stem cell surface marker with no connection to its role in photoreceptor outer segment morphogenesis or retinal dystrophy. Off-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Classic paper describing isolation and purification of bovine rod outer segment G-protein (transducin = GNAT1 alpha subunit) along with cGMP phosphodiesterase. Foundational biochemistry for GNAT1, directly describing the protein's properties and reconstitution with visual pigment membranes.

Directly maps receptor- and betagamma-binding surfaces on the alpha subunit of retinal transducin (GNAT1) using alanine-scanning mutagenesis of 100 mutants. Proposes a mechanism for receptor-catalyzed nucleotide exchange. Central to understanding GNAT1 structure-function.

Applies evolutionary trace analysis to identify functionally conserved binding surfaces on Galpha subunits, with direct application to transducin (GNAT1). The paper identifies receptor and effector interaction sites on the alpha subunit, proposing a structural model of the receptor-G protein complex. Relevant to GNAT1 signaling mechanism.

Studies combinatorial peptide library variants of the C-terminal 340-350 region of transducin alpha (GNAT1) that bind rhodopsin with high affinity and stabilize metarhodopsin II. Directly characterizes GNAT1-rhodopsin interaction surface and identifies critical residues. Core GNAT1 biochemistry.

Identifies a GTPase-accelerating factor for transducin in rod outer segment membranes (precursor work leading to RGS9 identification). Transducin alpha = GNAT1. The paper characterizes GNAT1 GTPase regulation in its native retinal context. Abstract is empty but the title is unambiguous.

Uses time-resolved light scattering to resolve the temporal sequence of Galpha and Ggamma C-terminal interactions with activated rhodopsin (R*) in native membranes. Gtalpha = GNAT1. Proposes a sequential coupling mechanism with direct implications for GNAT1 activation kinetics.

Cancer biology review of CD133 (PROM1) as a cancer stem cell biomarker covering signaling pathways and miRNA regulation in solid tumors. No retinal, photoreceptor, or ophthalmic content. PROM1 is relevant to the library only through its role in retinal outer segment disc morphogenesis and inherited macular/retinal dystrophies; this paper has no connection to that biology. Off-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Identifies constitutively activating mutations (Thr-325, Val-328, Phe-332) in the alpha5 helix of transducin alpha (GNAT1) that increase basal nucleotide exchange up to 165-fold. Directly characterizes GNAT1 activation mechanisms and identifies a functional microdomain mediating receptor-catalyzed exchange.

Epidemiological study of prevalence and inheritance patterns of congenital nystagmus in a Swedish population. FRMD7 mutations are the primary cause of X-linked idiopathic congenital nystagmus (NYS1). A population genetics study of congenital nystagmus is directly relevant to FRMD7 as the main causative gene for this phenotype.

Studies the inhibitory subunit of cGMP phosphodiesterase (Pgamma) interaction with transducin alpha (T alpha = GNAT1), demonstrating that Pgamma inhibits GTP hydrolysis by transducin and modulates T alpha-T betagamma reassociation. Directly characterizes how GNAT1 function is regulated by its effector interaction.

Uses ATR-FTIR spectroscopy to study binding of transducin (GNAT1 alpha subunit and derived C-terminal peptides) to rhodopsin. Abstract is absent but the title unambiguously describes transducin-rhodopsin interaction characterization, directly relevant to GNAT1 function.

Studies structural requirements in the C-terminal 340-350 peptide of transducin alpha (GNAT1) for stabilizing metarhodopsin II. Identifies critical residues (Cys-347, N-terminal charge effects) in GNAT1's receptor interaction domain. Core GNAT1-rhodopsin coupling biochemistry.

Directly demonstrates light adaptation-associated transcriptional up-regulation of Guca1a (GCAP1, the protein product of GUCA1A) and Guca1b (GCAP2) in isolated photoreceptors and retinas. GUCA1A is the tracked gene. The paper characterizes a novel gene-expression-level mechanism of light adaptation mediated by GUCA1A and provides ERG evidence of functional recovery, directly relevant to GUCA1A biology in photoreceptors.
